$comment: The app's key screens, captured from each platform's preview build: the iPhone's (#331) and Android's (#372). Each screen opens by deep link (sdachurchapp://<path>) after its settings are saved; each variant adds the settings listed under variants. A variant that changes one platform's own settings (iosTextSize on the iPhone; fontScale and displayScale on Android) is taken only there, and a screen with platforms only on those. Screenshots are named <platform>/<screen>-<variant>.png. checks lists automatic image checks for a screen, mustShowLines regular expressions that some line of its text must match (or { line, minLeft } for a line that must also start at least minLeft of the way across, such as right-aligned text), mustNotShowLines ones that no line may match, variantRules more of either for one variant (a rule written { line, platforms } applies on those platforms only, such as a line the Android phone's smaller screen leaves below the fold), and tabs false for a screen without the tab bar, such as the Bible while reading (scripts/check-screens.cjs); appStore lists, per App Store language, the iPhone shots to upload, in order, appStoreIpad the iPad's, from the screens that list ipadVariants (#324), and googlePlay, per Google Play language, the Android ones (at most 8). Each screen's group names the related screens it is captured with, on one of up to five runners at once (#453): put a new screen in the group for its part of the app, as groups describes. A test fails if a group would take more than 6 minutes. That limit is a reminder to prune, not a rule: first drop variants that repeat what another shot already shows and screens no longer worth a check, spend the time saved on screens and states no shot covers yet (#456), then move some related screens to a lighter group or split one, and if a group is still over after that, raise the limit. Leave out screens that show members' names or photos, such as the bulletin, the team page, the fellowship page, and the worship schedule. A path's popup= opens one of that screen's popups or dialogs, in the preview build only (#372); its shot skips the tab and verse-button checks, which the popup covers or dims. The Bible's play=1 starts its audio the same way (#551). A screen's record names what the app saves of such an action, which scripts/key-screen-records.cjs checks, saying when the network was the cause of a failure; later takes a second screenshot that many seconds after the first, <platform>/<screen>-<variant>-later.png; and mustAdvance is a regular expression for a time, its first two groups the minutes and seconds, that must have moved on in the later shot by at least half that time. See docs/operations/native-builds.md.

ipad.$comment: The iPad (#324): the 13-inch iPad Pro, whose screen is the size App Store Connect's iPad screenshots take. Only the screens that list ipadVariants are taken on it, on a runner of its own; its variants can turn it to landscape (orientation), which serve-sim does, since simctl can't. See "iPad key screens" in docs/operations/native-builds.md.

android.$comment: The emulator. phone is the best-selling Android phone of Q1 2026, the Samsung Galaxy A07 4G (Counterpoint), sold mostly in the Middle East, Africa, and Latin America, where most Adventists live: a 6.7-inch 720 × 1600 screen at 300 dpi, 384 × 853 dp. The US's best-selling Androids, the Galaxy A16 and A17, are 384 dp wide too, as this church's members' phones are likely to be. Google Play takes no screenshot taller than 2:1, so its shots are taken on a second emulator of googlePlay's size. google_apis, not google_apis_playstore, because the capture writes the app's settings as root. See "Android key screens" in docs/operations/native-builds.md.

splitWindows.$comment: The iPad's Split View and Slide Over windows, in points (dp at 2x, 320 dpi), taken on their own emulators (#324): Slide Over, and the 11-inch iPad's half, the 13-inch iPad's half in portrait, and its two-thirds in landscape.

groups.home: The Home tab and the pages it opens, other than the hymnals: Discover, About, and Give, and first-launch setup over it.
groups.bible-reading: The Bible reader's layout: one and two translations, the header and its back arrow, text scrolled under the status bar, the popup a tapped verse opens, and Offline Bible Audio, which its audio settings open.
groups.bible-text: What the Bible reader shows: Chinese, Cantonese, Simplified Chinese, pinyin, and Spanish text, long chapters, and Selah.
groups.library: The Explore tab and the Library: featured books, shelves, and each collection.
groups.worship-and-you: The hymnals, Sabbath School, and the You tab with its open-source licenses page and its Text size and Language dialogs. Also, on the iPhone only, Bible audio playing and a children's lesson open in Quick Look (#551): this group finished first or second in the six release runs from 2026-10-19 to 11-02, 1.5 to 7.5 minutes before the slowest, so these longer shots shouldn't lengthen the run.

screens.name: setup
screens.$comment: First-launch setup, which shows until has-completed-setup is saved: its first step of three (#523), the welcome and the language, with the step dots and Next below the scrolling part, so the way on stays in view. At the large size the step still fits. RapidOCR reads the white Next on its blue button as Net at the Android phone's default size, so there only the large variant requires it.

screens.name: home
screens.$comment: xl-ios-large-text and es-xl-ios-large-text: the app at 200% with the iPhone's accessibility-large text (2×), held to 3.2× by the combined cap, as with Android's largest font at 200%, where the tab labels used to wrap (#380); xl-android-font-max and es-xl-android-font-max are that case itself, with the same rules, except that the Android phone's narrower screen may wrap the heading between its words; and android-display-large is Android's largest display size. Their verse-card buttons and heading must show whole words, not “Shar” or “Versícul / o” (#385). The verse changes daily, and a long one, such as John 1:1 or Genesis 1:27 in English or most verses in Spanish, pushes one button or both below the shot, so no rule requires a button. English instead requires its heading whole on one line and fails on a line ending in a cut-off button word, such as “Shar” or “Rea”; Spanish requires its heading, with or without the accent, which OCR can miss when the photo's cross runs behind it. The tab-label check fails on a wrapped label, or one pushed up out of the tab bar's area by an overgrown bar. Not the iPhone's very largest size: at about 6× in all, page titles break mid-word, which isn't a useful baseline. es-large is Spanish at 150% on the phones: on the Android phone's 384 points, "Compartir" didn't fit beside Leer Versículo and broke mid-word, so the buttons stack wherever a word wouldn't fit (#324). The Sabbath countdown stays on the right in default and es-large, at least 40% of the way across: it goes below its label only when a word of the label, date, or place couldn't fit whole beside it (countdownFitsBeside), as at 170% or more on a 375-point iPhone in Spanish. zh and zh-cn: the countdown's date in Chinese, such as 11月6日星期五, which the iPhone's text recognition reads with a space before 星期. On Android, Hermes once showed the Simplified one in English ("Friday, November 6"), so the app writes Chinese dates out by hand (formatAppDate).

screens.name: bible-dual
screens.$comment: The header's translation button in full: the 文A icon (which Vision reads as XA, and RapidOCR as 文A, or as A alone at Android's largest font), the EN badge, and both names, not cut to B… or C… (#376). On the iPad, Vision can read the book button's chevron as part of its name, "Psalmsv".

screens.name: bible-dual-back
screens.$comment: Opened from Home, so the header also has a back arrow and less room. When it's tight, the translation button gives up its 文A icon first, then its names, cut short and then dropped, then its badges (#376). On the iPhone at 150% and 200% only the icon goes: the EN badge and both full names stay. The Android phone's narrower screen drops the names too, leaving EN + 繁, so there only the badge is required.

screens.name: bible-cuv
screens.$comment: Mandarin is the default narrator, so the audio button shows 國語.

screens.name: bible-cuv-cantonese
screens.$comment: With the Cantonese narrator chosen, the audio button shows 粵語.

screens.name: bible-cuv-after-spanish
screens.$comment: The Spanish Bible was open with the CUV underneath, then a link opens the CUV. Its book names must replace the Spanish ones, which once stayed until a restart (#373). The interface is English, as when the bug showed, so Vision reads the dock in English first and misses 詩篇; it reads a stale Salmos reliably.

screens.name: bible-cuvs
screens.$comment: Simplified characters, so the audio button shows 国语.

screens.name: bible-scrolled
screens.$comment: Opens at John 3:14, so earlier verses sit under the status bar; checks it stays clear.

screens.name: bible-verse-popup
screens.$comment: The popup a tapped verse opens, opened by popup=verse in the preview build (#372): the reference as its title beside an X, with no Close button (#464). A popup covers or dims the tab bar and chapter controls, so those aren't checked. The original-language Greek ships with the app, so its credit must show, with the license CC BY 4.0 requires (it may wrap onto its own line). Vision reads the share icon before Share Verse as <.

screens.name: bible-search
screens.$comment: Whole-Bible search (#516), opened by search= in the key-screens build, as the capture can't type. Genesis 22 is open, so its match for Moriah comes first, then the whole Bible's two by book, with counts. OCR may read the · between a heading and its count as another mark, so the rules allow any. The results are a page of their own, over the reader's Verse button and the tab bar, which used to show through them.

screens.name: bible-audio-settings
screens.$comment: The audio settings popup, opened by popup=audio-settings in the preview build (#372): its title beside an X (#464), and the CUV's two audio languages, in English (the Google Play screenshot) and Chinese. The audio button behind it shows 國語, so the rules require lines only the popup shows. Vision misses the lone 粵語 label, so the Cantonese row is found by its credit, WordProject. It's centred like the other popups: until 1.3.2 it sat at the bottom, its title 47% of the way down where theirs are at 25 to 32%, so the title must be no farther down than 40%. Under the audio languages, Listen offline is one row that opens Offline Bible Audio in the You tab, where Bible audio is downloaded and deleted (#556); it must show, though the Android phone's shorter popup may leave the row below the fold.

screens.name: offline-bible-audio
screens.$comment: Offline Bible Audio, where Bible audio is downloaded and deleted (#556), as the Bible's audio settings open it for Souer's English narration: the narrator, named language first (the user: people don't know who Souer is), then the whole Bible, the Old Testament, and its sections, closed, each with its book count and size. A key-screen build has nothing downloaded, so no row offers delete. The text readers may read a closed section's chevron with its title ("> Law") and drop the spaces in "英語 – Souer" and "66 卷", so the rules allow both.

screens.name: offline-bible-audio-narrator
screens.$comment: Offline Bible Audio's narrator popup, which lists every narrator to download with what's on the phone, by popup=narrator in the preview build (#324). A key-screen build has nothing downloaded. Its iPad shot checks the popup's width: when it was new, it had a percentage width, which on iOS fills 90% of an iPad.

screens.name: bible-audio-download-tip
screens.$comment: The audio settings popup as the marked audio button opens it when playback keeps stopping to load (#595), by popup=audio-download-tip in the preview build. The BSB has four narrators above Listen offline, so the popup scrolls down to it: the tip's line, and the Offline Bible Audio row below it, which opens the downloads (#556), must show. The line doesn't say "keeps stopping", which Android's check reserves for the system's crash dialog. On the iPad, the dimmed page shows beside the popup, and Vision can read its words into the tip's line, so the rule finds the tip anywhere in a line.

screens.name: bible-long-chapter
screens.$comment: Psalm 119 from verse 100, for three-digit verse numbers at large text sizes. RapidOCR may read a verse number without the space after it, as 102I, so the rules only require no further digit.

screens.name: bible-higgaion-selah
screens.$comment: Psalm 9:16 in the BSB ends with "Higgaion Selah", plain text after the verse's poetry lines in the HelloAO data. At the default text size the reader shows it right-aligned under the verse, so it must start in the right half of the screen.

screens.name: bible-selah
screens.$comment: Psalm 9:20 in the BSB ends with "Selah" alone, right-aligned on its own line, so it must start in the right half of the screen. The rule needs a line starting with Selah, so 9:16's "Higgaion Selah" can't satisfy it.

screens.name: explore
screens.$comment: xl-ios-large-text and es-xl-ios-large-text check the tab labels at about 4× text, as on Home (#380), and their Android counterparts at Android's largest font. xl-android-font-max is also the Android counterpart of max. max is the app at 200% with the iPhone's very largest text, about 6× before the combined cap (MAX_COMBINED_TEXT_SCALE) held it to 3.2×; at 6× the Library card's title read "Libr". In Chinese the Library is 精選書庫 (hand-picked library), and the In-depth Bible Study card for the SDA Bible app shows below Spotify; it's Chinese only, since the app's commentary and nearly all its books are Chinese (#554).

screens.name: library
screens.$comment: The featured carousel's arrows sit beside its dots, under the carousel, so they never cover its first book's title (#447): The Bruised Reed in every language, whole on one line, right of the cover. The shelf below wraps the same title after The Bruised, so only the carousel's line matches. Vision isn't asked to read the arrows: a chevron alone in a circle is no reliable text.

screens.name: library-contemporary
screens.$comment: Chinese readers get a shelf of today's Adventist writers, books the church's leaders chose from the Chinese Union Mission's reader, titled in the app's script; the covers are the reader's, in Simplified. The Traditional shelf title and 地上的最後一夜 (最后 on its cover) can only come from the app's own text (#554). The second row's titles are below the fold on both phones.

screens.name: library-children
screens.$comment: Books by other writers lead the Children shelf, and Ellen G. White's books for adults stay on her own shelf (#391).

screens.name: library-youth
screens.$comment: Pastor Hsi leads the Youth shelf, ahead of Ellen G. White's books, and The Pilgrim's Progress follows in each reader's language: its 1869 Mandarin edition for Chinese readers, and Chapel Library's for Spanish (#391). Its English and Spanish titles wrap, differently on each phone, so only their first words are checked.

screens.name: sabbath-school
screens.$comment: The adult lessons with this week's mission video between them (#508), in each language. The card's description names a different Sabbath each week, so only its title is checked, by its first words, since the Android phone wraps the Spanish one. In Chinese the title is 本週聖工剪影, or the Sabbath of the last Mandarin video the phone found, such as 10月31日聖工剪影. The card pushes the first children's age group, checked here before (#338), below the fold on the iPhone too.

screens.name: sabbath-school-lesson-download
screens.$comment: The popup a tap on a children's lesson opens while its PDF downloads (#529). Key screens can't tap, so a key-screens build opens it from popup=, with a fixed 5.1 of 14.2 MB. The iPhone's text recognition reads "14.2MB", without the space.

screens.name: sabbath-school-lesson-offline
screens.$comment: The same popup offline with no copy of the lesson (#529, part of #533): it says so, with only the X, in Chinese.

screens.name: sabbath-school-lesson-viewer
screens.$comment: A children's lesson downloaded and open in Quick Look, the iPhone's own viewer (#529, #551). popup=lesson-viewer opens the Beginner student lesson in a key-screens build as a tap would: this week's PDF is about 1 MB. The app records how it opened (record), and the capture fails unless Quick Look opened, saying whether the network was the cause. Where the week's lesson has no PDF yet, the browser opens its website instead and the run only warns, so the rules accept that page's address too. Nothing of the page beneath may show.

screens.name: bible-audio-playing
screens.$comment: Bible audio playing on the iPhone (#551), which nothing else checks before release: Android's is checked by android-audio-e2e.yml. play=1 starts Psalm 23's Mandarin recording in a key-screens build as a tap on Play would. A second screenshot is taken later seconds after the first, and the elapsed time left of the timeline must have moved on by at least half that (mustAdvance). The player's own status is recorded too (record): if it didn't play, the capture says whether this runner could reach the audio's hosts, so a network failure reads as one. The lock screen's 10- and 30-second skips can't be pressed in the Simulator; test/bible-audio-service.test.ts checks what the app passes them.

screens.name: hymnal-selection
screens.$comment: The hymnal page (#413): a carousel of the hymnals, the app language's first, then the picked hymnal's search and its hymns, each 1985 or 505 hymn with the other hymnal's number, a verse chip beside it (an English hymn's own, and a 505 hymn's 1985 equivalent's in Chinese, such as 詩篇 100 on 505's 1), and the 1985 and 505 hymns' Piano only videos (#424). Vision reads the 文A icon in a chip as XA and a row's treble clef as a character, so those lines are matched anywhere.

screens.name: hymnal
screens.$comment: A link to one hymn, as from the bulletin: the hymnal page opens on the SDA Hymnal with just that hymn, marked, its Chinese 505 number, its With singing and Piano only videos (#424), and Show all hymns. At the app's 200% text size the Chinese 505 · 16 chip must still show its whole number (a long label wraps inside the chip), and the buttons stack, so they and Show all hymns may fall below the shot. The hymnal's name and the hymn's title wrap at 200% too, so there only their first words are required.

screens.name: hymnal-chinese
screens.$comment: An older hymnal route with an old search, highlight=平安夜, opens the hymnal page with that hymnal picked: the 506, not the 505 a Chinese interface would show first, its cover photo cropped to the carousel's 2:3 frame. Its one match, 82, comes first, with its recording labeled 演唱 (With singing) although the 506 has no piano videos yet, then the heading over the matches in the other hymnals, each under its hymnal's name, the 505's 66 first (on the phones: in the iPad's landscape shot, at 150%, it's below the fold), and no longer the hymnal's short name on each result's own line ("505", "1985", "707 新編簡譜"). Vision may read "82. 平安夜" without the space, may read the dash in a hymnal's name as 一, and reads the YouTube logo before 演唱 as a character.

screens.name: discover
screens.$comment: xl-ios-large-text: the app at 200% with the iPhone's accessibility-large text, held to 3.2× by the combined cap. The two-column cards' titles stay at the default 1.25× (#387), so "About Denomination" must keep "Denomination" whole instead of breaking it as "Den / omination". xl-android-font-max is the same case on Android, at its largest font. es-default-text is Spanish at the app's default 125%: on the Android phone's 384 points, "Compañerismo" was wider than its card's title, so each card shrinks its grid's text just enough to keep the widest word whole (#324). Its ñ may read as another letter.

screens.name: give
screens.$comment: Zelle stays hidden until its address is ready (#392). When shown, its heading sits just above the tab bar.

screens.name: you
screens.$comment: Share the App, the first item under About & Support, opens a QR code a friend can scan to download the app (#555). Help & Feedback, after it, emails the technology team (#541). Offline Bible Audio, the last setting, lists the Bible audio downloaded for listening offline (#556); the web has none. It pushes About & Support down, so on the Android phone's shorter screen Share the App and Help & Feedback may fall below the screenshot: they're checked on the iPhone only.

screens.name: share-app
screens.$comment: The Share the App popup, opened by popup=share-app (#555): an X beside its title, the download page's QR code on white so it scans in the dark theme too, the address, and Share Link, with no Close button. The QR image has no text, so the rules require the address and the button. The button's share icon reads as "<" before its label, so the label isn't anchored at the start.

screens.name: text-size
screens.$comment: The Text size dialog, opened by popup=text-size (#372): an X beside its title, and Reset the only button at its foot, with no Apply, since a size takes effect as it changes (#464). At 200% its text runs past the popups' height limit (POPUP_MAX_HEIGHT_FRACTION in styles/PopupStyles.ts), so the dialog stops there and its text scrolls, leaving room around it to tap. Its title is also on the You screen behind it, so the rules require lines only the dialog shows. The iPad saves no text size, so its shot shows the size a tablet starts at, 150%, and Reset returns there (#324).

screens.name: language
screens.$comment: The Language dialog, opened by popup=language (#372): an X beside its title and no Close button (#464). Its title is also on the You screen behind it, so the rules require the options' descriptions, which only the dialog shows.

screens.name: licenses
screens.$comment: The legal disclaimer moved to the website (#412); the open-source notices stay in the app, on this screen.
